extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, investigators, research administrators, and institutional officials
extracted.subtask_short: NIH grant policy news for applicants
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH policy updates, resources, and reminders relevant to preparing and submitting grant applications (model selection, data management plans, reproducibility, review outcomes, and program changes). Useful for applicants and institutional administrators to stay current on procedural and expectation changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting research models (including New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions; NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From page text: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions." Use NAMs where scientifically appropriate but prioritize model choice that best addresses the research question and translational relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans, use the new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From page text: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans." Applicants should follow the new format and required elements when submitting DMS plans for applicable applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and awards are expected to support reliability of biomedical research by embedding replication and reproducibility practices; NIH is promoting replication and reproducibility through the Gold Standard Science plan and a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From page text: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational... NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise." Applicants should consider replication/reproducibility in study design, justification, and proposed activities where relevant; watch for initiative-specific funding or highlighted topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following temporary review modifications, the middle third of applications in a study section may be designated as 'competitive but not discussed' — indicating that strong applications can fall below the cut-off for discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From page text: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'" This describes NIH's triage/scoring practice during that period; applicants receiving this designation are competitive but were not selected for discussion due to cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — follow application format and note possible splitting into linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: For the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure, applicants should learn key features and the application format; applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From page text: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests." Applicants should follow the PF5 application format and be aware of the possibility of post-review splitting into linked awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of centralized NIH peer review within CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH consolidated peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR); applicants should be aware this centralization affects peer review processes, with goals of improving efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From page text: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)... As the one-year anniversary approaches, we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process." Applicants and institutional offices should account for centralized review processes and any resulting procedural or timing changes.
